title: WPSB/206/2019 of ASHOK KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE SRI RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN
AND
THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE ALOK KUMAR VERMA
20TH SEPTEMBER, 2021
WRIT PETITION (S/B) No. 206 of 2019
Between:
Ashok Kumar.
...Petitioner
and
State of Uttarakhand and others.

: Mr. R.C. Tamta, the learned counsel.
Counsel for the respondent nos.
1 and 2.
: Mr. Pradeep Joshi, the learned Additional
Chief Standing Counsel for the State of
Uttarakhand.
Counsel for the respondent nos.
3 to 5.
: Dr. Kartikey Hari Gupta, the learned
counsel.
Counsel for the respondent nos.
6 and 7.
: Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, the learned Senior
Counsel assisted by Mr. Shubhang Dobhal,
the learned counsel.
The Court made the following :
JUDGMENT : (per Hon'ble The Chief Justice Sri Raghvendra Singh Chauhan)
 This Writ Petition has been filed by the petitioner
for seeking the following reliefs:-

2
i. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
certiorari, quashing the impugned order no. 5594 dated
23.04.2016, passed by respondent no.5.
ii. Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus, commanding/directing the respondents to
give the appointment or approval to the selection of
Assistant Professor (Maths) without any further delay,
whenever the selection committee selected the petitioner
as the Assistant Professor (Maths) in Shri Guru Ram Rai
(P.G.) College, Dehradun.
2. Briefly, the facts of the case are that, in 2010,
the Principal, Shri Guru Ram Rai (P.G.) College, the
respondent No. 7, invited applications from the eligible
candidates for the post of Assistant Professor in various
departments. The petitioner applied for the post of
Assistant Professor (Maths) under the Scheduled Caste
category. However, after the lapse of five years, the
respondents did not proceed further with the selection
process.
3. Again, on 05.05.2015, the respondent No. 7
invited applications from the eligible candidates for the post
of Assistant Professor in different subject in the various
departments of the Guru Ram Rai (P.G.) College. According
to the advertisement, a candidate must possess good
academic record with at least 55% marks in the Post-Graduation, and must possess a Ph.D. degree, and the

3
candidates who qualified the NET examination in
accordance with the University Grants Commission
Regulations, 2009, would be exempted from the
requirement of the minimum eligibility condition. It was
also clarified in the advertisement dated 05.05.2015 that
the candidates who have already applied pursuant to the
advertisement issued in the year 2010, need not to apply
again. Their candidature will be considered. The petitioner
was allowed to participate in the selection process as per
the advertisement issued on 05.05.2015. Subsequently, on
04.12.2015, a call letter was issued to the petitioner by
respondent No. 6 for participating in the interview, which
was scheduled to be held on 04.01.2016. The Selection
Committee duly selected the petitioner for the post of
Assistant Professor (Maths) in its meeting dated
04.01.2016.
4. On 06.02.2016, the respondent No. 6 sent a
letter to the Vice-Chancellor, Hemwati Nandan Bahuguna
Garhwal University, the respondent No. 3, for approval of
the selection of the selected candidates for the post of
Assistant Professor (Maths) in the respondent-College; the
name of petitioner was at Sl. No. 2 under the reserved

4
category. On 11.03.2016, the Joint Registrar of the H.N.B
Garhwal University sent a letter to the respondent No. 7
regarding the approval of one Mr. Vivek Kumar, as
Assistant Professor (Maths) under the General category.
However, by letter dated 23.04.2016, the respondent No. 5
informed the respondent No. 7 that the approval for
selection of the petitioner for the post of Assistant Professor
(Maths) cannot be granted due to the non-fulfillment of the
educational qualification as per the conditions of the
Government Order dated 27.02.2007.
5. In the counter-affidavit filed by the respondent
Nos. 3 to 5, it is stated that the Management of the College
had also recommended the name of the petitioner under
the reserved category, despite the fact that the petitioner,
admittedly, secured only 44.27% marks in B.Sc. But,
according to the requirement, as prescribed in the Statute
and clarified by the Government, vide its order dated
27.02.2007, is that a candidate belonging to the general
category must possess 50% marks in Graduation, and the
candidates belonging to the reserved category must
possess 45% marks in Graduation. The said G.O. further
clarified that for rounding off the marks obtained by a

5
General Category candidate above 49.5% would be treated
as 50%, and for the Reserved Category Candidates marks
obtained 44.5% be treated as 45%. However, the
petitioner has secured only 44.27% marks in his
Graduation, which is less than the minimum prescribed
marks for the Reserved Category candidate.
6. Mr. R.C. Tamta, the learned counsel for the
petitioner, has raised the following contentions before this
Court :-
 Firstly, the petitioner happens to be the only
candidate belonging to the Scheduled Caste community.
Therefore, a liberal view should have been taken by the
respondent no. 5.
 Secondly, although the petitioner has scored only
44.27% in his graduation degree, but the fact remains that
in his M.Sc. he had scored 53.30%, he had completed his
Ph.D. and had qualified NET. Thus, instead of considering
his marks for B.Sc. and disqualifying him on the said basis,
the respondent no. 5 should have considered his higher
qualifications and his marks in M.Sc. and the fact that he

6
has qualified NET, and has done his Ph.D. Therefore, the
impugned order dated 23.04.2016 deserves to be set aside
by this Court.
7. However, on the other hand, Dr. Kartikey Hari
Gupta, the learned counsel for the respondent nos. 3 to 5,
has raised the following counter-contentions before this
Court:-
 Firstly, according to the Government Order dated
27.02.2007, it was made abundantly clear that the
candidates belonging to the reserved category must have a
minimum of 45% in graduation degree. It was further
clarified that in case a candidate scores 44.5%, then the
number would be rounded off to 45%. However, in the
present case, the petitioner has scored only 44.27%.
Therefore, his marks cannot be rounded off to 45%, as his
marks are below 44.5%.
 Secondly, merely because he happens to be the
only candidate from the Scheduled Caste category, the said
fact would not permit the respondents to violate the
Government Order dated 27.02.2007.

7
 Thirdly, once the eligibility requirements are
prescribed, and it is clearly stated that a candidate must
have 45% in his graduation degree, the fact that the
petitioner has higher degrees, such as M.Sc. and Ph.D.,
would not make him eligible for the post of Assistant
Professor (Maths). Therefore, the respondents are well
justified in passing the impugned order dated 23.04.2016.
Hence, the learned counsel has supported the impugned
order.
8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties, and
perused the record.
9. It is, indeed, trite to state that once the eligibility
criteria have been prescribed by the employer, a candidate
must possess the prescribed eligibility. Even if he is short
by a 0.1%, the respondents would be justified in concluding
that the person is ineligible.
10. Admittedly, the eligibility requirement prescribes
that a candidate belonging to the Scheduled Caste category
must have a minimum of 45% marks in his graduation

8
degree. Undoubtedly, the petitioner has merely 44.27%
marks in his graduation degree. This said 0.27% marks
cannot be possibly rounded off to make the marks as 45%.
Thus, without any doubt, the petitioner does not have the
minimum requisite marks of 45% in his B.Sc. degree. Even
if the petitioner has scored 53.06% marks in his M.Sc.
degree, has qualified NET, and has completed his Ph.D.,
even then this fact would not make him eligible as per the
prescribed criteria. Therefore, the respondents were
justified in passing the impugned order dated 23.04.2016.
11. Merely because the petitioner happens to be the
only candidate belonging to the Scheduled Caste
community, he is unjustified in claiming that the law should
be violated in his favour. According to the Government
Order dated 27.02.2007, a concession was already made in
favour of the reserved category candidates. While the
general category candidates were required to have 50% in
the graduation degree, those belonging to the reserved
category were required to have merely 45% in their
graduation degree. Thus, the petitioner is unjustified in
claiming that even further concession should be made in his
favour ostensibly on the ground that he happens to be the

9
sole candidate from the reserved category. Such a stand
taken by the learned counsel for the petitioner is highly
misplaced.
12. For the reasons stated above, this Court does not
find any merit in the present Writ Petition. It is, hereby,
dismissed.
13. No order as to cost.
_____________________________
RAGHVENDRA SINGH CHAUHAN, C.J.
___________________
ALOK KUMAR VERMA, J.
Dt: 20th September, 2021
Rahul
